chunks: And among what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Allah would not make menstruation together with pregnancy. That is, if a woman sees blood while she is pregnant, she does not leave the salat (prayer), unless she sees it at the head of the child, when labor pains strike her and she sees blood; then she leaves the salat (prayer).”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The way to reconcile these reports is that when a pregnant woman sees blood according to her usual pattern from times other than the days of pregnancy, and it has not changed and has not been withheld from her from that time except by the measure of a day or two, then she leaves the salat (prayer), breaks the sawm (fasting), and the ruling of a menstruating woman applies to her equally. But if she sees blood after it had been withheld from her customary time for twenty days or more, and then she sees blood, then she prays and fasts, and her ruling is not the ruling of a menstruating woman. And that which indicates this detailed distinction...

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman, the basis of the legal ruling discussed here
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), which may be left or maintained depending on the ruling of the blood
key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: sawm (fasting), whose ruling follows the determination of menstruation or otherwise
key_terms.الْحَائِضِ: a menstruating woman, whose legal status is the point of comparison
key_terms.حَيْضًا: menstruation; the legal state that suspends certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: If a pregnant woman sees blood, does she stop salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of blood seen by a pregnant woman and its relation to menstruation, salat (prayer), and sawm (fasting). It also includes Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s reconciliation of differing reports by distinguishing between blood that appears near a woman’s normal cycle and blood that appears after a much longer interruption.
